items.stem:
The picture shows some of the bones in the human body.

Match each labelled part to the name of the bone.
items.note: Mark scheme: A–skull, B–jaw, C–rib; all three correct = 1 mark.

items.stem:
Complete the sentence about the leg bones.

The leg bones move because they have …… of muscles attached to them.
items.note: Mark scheme: pairs. Printed as the first blank of Question 1(b) [2]; each correct answer = 1 mark.

items.stem:
Complete the sentence about the leg bones.

The leg bones move when the muscles contract and …….
items.note: Mark scheme: relax. Do not accept stretch. Printed as the second blank of Question 1(b) [2]; each correct answer = 1 mark.

items.stem:
Carlos asks his friends to name the planets in the Solar System.

He records the number of planets each friend names in a dot plot.

Write down the total number of friends Carlos asks to name the planets.
items.note: Mark scheme: 19

items.stem:
Look at the same dot plot.

How many friends name all the planets in the Solar System?
items.note: Mark scheme: 5

items.stem:
Planetary systems contain stars and planets.

Write down one other structure found in planetary systems.
items.note: Mark scheme: asteroids or comets. Accept any other named structure in a planetary system, e.g. moon. Ignore stars or planets. A person should check this answer against the mark scheme.

items.stem:
Blessy investigates electrical circuits.

The diagram shows the equipment she uses.

Blessy uses component X to light up the lamp.

Write down the name of component X.
items.note: Mark scheme: switch

items.stem:
Blessy puts a second lamp into her electrical circuit.

Predict what happens to the brightness of the first lamp.
items.note: Mark scheme: (idea of) becomes dimmer. Accept goes out or does not light up. A person should check this answer against the mark scheme.

items.stem:
Blessy makes a gap in her first electrical circuit.

Blessy puts different objects in the gap to complete the electrical circuit. She records if the lamp lights up.

Here are her results.

object A: lamp lights up – yes
object B: no
object C: yes
object D: no
object E: yes
object F: yes

How many objects make the lamp light up?
items.note: Mark scheme: 4

items.stem:
Object B is a plastic spoon.

Complete the sentence to explain the result for object B.

The plastic spoon is a good electrical …… and a poor electrical (see next question).
items.note: Mark scheme: insulator. Printed as the first blank of Question 3(d) [2]; each correct answer = 1 mark.

items.stem:
Object B is a plastic spoon.

Complete the sentence to explain the result for object B.

The plastic spoon is a good electrical insulator and a poor electrical …….
items.note: Mark scheme: conductor. Printed as the second blank of Question 3(d) [2]; each correct answer = 1 mark.

items.stem:
Mia has a frozen ice lolly.

She leaves the ice lolly in a warm room.

The picture shows the ice lolly at the start and after five minutes.

Describe two differences between the ice lolly at the start and the ice lolly after five minutes.

1
2

accepted: the lolly after five minutes is smaller
the frozen lolly is not melted
the lolly after five minutes has melted
the frozen lolly has the stick visible at one end only
the lolly after five minutes has the stick visible at both ends
there is no liquid around the frozen lolly
there is liquid around the lolly after five minutes
the frozen lolly is bigger and it has not melted
the lolly after five minutes is smaller and has melted

items.note: Mark scheme: any two from — frozen lolly is bigger; frozen lolly is not melted / lolly after 5 minutes has melted; stick visible at one end only / at both ends; they are different shapes; no liquid around the frozen lolly / liquid around the lolly after five minutes. Accept the reverse argument. 1 mark each. A person should check this answer against the mark scheme.

items.stem:
The frozen ice lolly is a solid at the start.

Complete the sentence to explain why the solid ice lolly in the warm room changes.

The warm room …… the solid ice lolly.
items.note: Mark scheme: melts. Accept heats (up). Printed as the first blank of Question 4(b) [2]; each correct answer = 1 mark.

items.stem:
Complete the sentence.

The solid ice lolly changes state to become a …….
items.note: Mark scheme: liquid. Printed as the second blank of Question 4(b) [2]; each correct answer = 1 mark.

items.stem:
Change of state is a type of process.

Choose the name of this process.
items.note: Mark scheme: physical (paper: circle the name; more than one circled = 0).

items.stem:
The picture shows two food chains.

Which word describes the plants in the food chains?
items.note: Mark scheme: producer (paper: circle the correct answer; more than one circled = 0).

items.stem:
Look at the same two food chains.

The mouse in each food chain is the same type of mouse.

Explain why this type of mouse is an omnivore.

accepted: it eats both plants and animals
the mouse eats plants and animals
it eats plants and it eats insects
because it eats plants and animals
because it eats plants and insects

items.note: Mark scheme: eats plants and animals. Accept eats plants and insects. A person should check this answer against the mark scheme.

items.stem:
Look at the same two food chains.

Write down the name of one carnivore from the food chains.
items.note: Mark scheme: owl

items.stem:
The owl has a backbone.

Write down the word that describes animals with backbones.
items.note: Mark scheme: vertebrate(s)

items.stem:
The diagram shows the parts of a volcano.

Match each labelled part to the name of the part.
items.note: Mark scheme: A–ash cloud, B–lava, C–magma, D–crater. All four correct = 2 marks; two or three correct = 1 mark; one correct = 0 marks.

items.stem:
Complete the sentence about volcanoes.

Volcanoes are found at breaks in the Earth's …….
items.note: Mark scheme: crust

items.stem:
Class 4 have a quiz about solids and liquids.

Their teacher gives them five sentences.

Select every sentence that is TRUE. Leave the false sentences unselected.
options: 1. Solids keep their shape because the particles are held together.
2. The particles in solids move faster than the particles in liquids.
3. Liquids change their shape because the particles move around.
4. Solids are easily compressed because their particles are close together.
5. Liquids have a fixed volume because their particles are held close together.

correct: 1. Solids keep their shape because the particles are held together.
3. Liquids change their shape because the particles move around.
5. Liquids have a fixed volume because their particles are held close together.

items.note: Mark scheme: 1 true, 2 false, 3 true, 4 false, 5 true. All five correct = 2 marks; three or four correct = 1 mark; one or two correct = 0 marks. Paper uses true/false tick boxes for each sentence.

items.stem:
Some solids behave like liquids.

Choose one solid that behaves like a liquid.
items.note: Mark scheme: sugar (paper: circle one; more than one circled = 0).

items.stem:
The picture shows Pierre watching a television.

The television is plugged into the mains electricity.

Pierre sees the image and hears the television.

This is because electrical energy is transferred into two types of energy.

One of these two types of energy is light energy.

Name the other type of energy.
items.note: Mark scheme: sound

items.stem:
Some of the electrical energy is lost to the surroundings.

This makes the television warmer.

Name the type of energy that makes the television warmer.
items.note: Mark scheme: heat. Accept thermal.

items.stem:
Complete the sentence about why Pierre sees the image on the television.

The light from the image travels in …… lines to his eyes.
items.note: Mark scheme: straight

items.stem:
Pierre switches the television off.

He still sees the television but not the image.

Explain why he still sees the television.

accepted: the television reflects light from another light source into his eyes
the television reflects light from another light source
light from another source reflects off the television into his eyes
light from the room reflects off the television
light reflects off the television into his eyes
light from a lamp reflects off the television
light is reflected from the television

items.note: Mark scheme: (idea that) the television reflects light from another light source (into his eyes). A person should check this answer against the mark scheme.
